facets.name: Property
facets.question: What characteristic is measured or styled?

facets.name: Element
facets.question: What abstract, nonspecific styling target is addressed?

facets.name: Attribute
facets.question: What aspect of the target is addressed?

facets.name: Prominence
facets.question: What visual emphasis is expressed, independently of shown or hidden behavior?

facets.name: Role
facets.question: What semantic intent does the styling communicate?

facets.name: Scale index
facets.question: What finite numeric coordinate identifies the source scale step?

facets.name: Number
facets.question: What positive safe integer identifies the numbered choice or part?

facets.name: Color name
facets.question: Which authored color source is referenced?

facets.name: Surface name
facets.question: Which authored surface source is referenced?

concepts.definition: A color value of the specified target and aspect; not a second color owner or a text-only quantity.
counterexamples: Color as a token family or Element

concepts.definition: The degree of opacity of the specified target and aspect, under its declared value and unit contract.
The nominal size of the declared target. For Text this is the nominal font size, not measured text width or height; its font metric and units must be explicit.
examples: Text Size with explicit nominal font-size metric and px units

concepts.definition: Inset space between a target boundary and its content. An axis or side is supplied explicitly when the measurement is directional.
examples: Horizontal Padding with reviewed inset endpoints

concepts.definition: An abstract rendered text target, independent of a particular typographic component or component-owned part.
An abstract rendered visual or graphic target, independent of a particular component entity.
counterexamples: A component identity inferred from its illustration

concepts.definition: An abstract workflow icon target. Component-owned icon parts reference this single shared meaning.
examples: A button icon part referencing Workflow-icon
counterexamples: A second Workflow-icon definition under Anatomy

concepts.definition: An abstract system UI icon target, including chevrons, checkmarks and close icons. Component parts reference this single shared meaning.
counterexamples: Separate UI and Icon terms inferred by splitting the compound

concepts.definition: An abstract bar target, including a divider, progress bar or slider track; not the interactive handle.
An entire interactive element such as a switch, slider handle, checkbox or radio; not an old nesting role or an entire composite component by assumption.
The background aspect of the declared target, styled by a separate Property such as Color or Opacity.
The boundary or border aspect of the declared target, styled by a separate Property such as Color or Opacity.
Elevated visual emphasis, independent of Accent color intent, Selected condition and shown or hidden behavior.
examples: Emphasized prominence with an independently declared color role

concepts.definition: An accent color role; not a synonym for Emphasized prominence or Selected interactive context.
counterexamples: Accent inferred only from an isSelected option

concepts.definition: A selected interactive condition, independent of visual prominence and semantic color role.
examples: A selected control with an independently chosen prominence
counterexamples: Selected inferred only from an accent color value

retired.reason: Retired boundary classification. Review the actual inset and axis before mapping to Padding.
Retired generic target. Define the real owned part or specific reusable pattern before mapping.
Retired generic nesting classification. Review the real pattern or component-owned part without inventing a replacement.
Old Object Content maps to Text only when the actual source context establishes a text target.
Fill is Color of the actual target and aspect; the target must be established before migration.

limitations: This is a proposed shared profile, not an adopted upstream specification.
A matching spelling is not proof of meaning. Text bindings require the shared definition and reviewed facet/type; other definitions remain non-standard.
Source-reference categories remain provisional under EPIC-3.2; labels cannot imply semantic classifications.
Component catalog migration does not change saved native Element assignments automatically.
Focus and Hover concurrency, Focus ownership, Subtle/Subdued and remaining facets require explicit review.
Review annotations are derived and versioned export data, not extra canonical token concepts or saved mode values.
